hypothesis: Remove one database round trip per callback claim to reduce simulator database work; claim SQL is not proven to be the sole cause of the 84/s backlog
change: One atomic SKIP LOCKED CTE UPDATE RETURNING replaces the locked SELECT plus lease UPDATE; acknowledgement, lease TTL, token fencing and financial logic unchanged

local_comparison.scope: Local PostgreSQL alternating rollback-only claim microbenchmark; no HTTP, customer load or capacity inference

baseline_claim.select:
SELECT p.*,o.total,o.currency,clock_timestamp() AS claim_observed_at FROM payment_attempts p JOIN orders o ON o.id=p.order_id
            WHERE p.deliveries<p.target_deliveries AND p.due_at<=clock_timestamp()
            AND (p.lease_until IS NULL OR p.lease_until<clock_timestamp())
            ORDER BY p.due_at LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE OF p SKIP LOCKED
baseline_claim.update: UPDATE payment_attempts SET lease_until=clock_timestamp()+interval '15 seconds',lease_token=%s WHERE id=%s

initial_new_suite.finding: Test fixture initially asserted tickets before consuming the persisted OrderPaid event; corrected to perform actual event-driven fulfillment and replay

native_checks: 24 simultaneous claims, one dispatch and one paid/issued ticket
two simulator SQL statements, HTTP outside claim transaction
stale lease token cannot acknowledge replacement
lost claim commit response sends no HTTP; existing lease expiry permits recovery
duplicate callbacks and OrderPaid replay issue one ticket

limits: Rollback-only local query timing is not a durable-commit or customer-throughput benchmark
No 84/s, flash-sale opening, post-TTL cloud queue drain or hourly qualification executed
No claim of 40-percent overall improvement or 300000 paid-issued tickets/hour
